record.original_question: For generic holomorphic foliations on the complex projective plane P2, what is the topology of a generic leaf?

evidence.quote: In the field of holomorphic foliations, even in P2, the following are examples of open basic questions : Do leaves always cluster at singular points ? What is the topology of generic leaves ? Are leaves dense for generic foliations ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the space of singular holomorphic foliations of a fixed degree $d \geq 2$ on the complex projective plane $\mathbb{P}^2(\mathbb{C})$. Such a foliation $\mathcal{F}$ is given, in homogeneous coordinates, by a polynomial vector field (up to multiples of the radial field) and has a finite singular set $\mathrm{Sing}(\mathcal{F})$; outside $\mathrm{Sing}(\mathcal{F})$ the foliation partitions $\mathbb{P}^2 \setminus \mathrm{Sing}(\mathcal{F})$ into immersed Riemann surfaces called leaves. The space of degree-$d$ foliations on $\mathbb{P}^2$ is itself a complex projective space, so one may speak of properties holding for a generic (i.e. on a residual or full-measure subset) foliation.

Determine the topology of a generic leaf for a generic holomorphic foliation on $\mathbb{P}^2(\mathbb{C})$. More precisely, describe the homeomorphism type (e.g. genus, number of ends, fundamental group) of the leaf through a generic point $p \in \mathbb{P}^2$ for a foliation $\mathcal{F}$ chosen generically in the space of degree-$d$ foliations.
artifact.status_search_result: The topology of generic leaves of a generic holomorphic foliation on $\mathbb{P}^2$ is widely cited as an open basic question in the theory of holomorphic foliations. Partial results exist in related settings: for generic foliations on Stein manifolds, Firsova showed all but countably many leaves are contractible (the rest cylinders), and for $\mathbb{P}^k$ it is known generic leaves are hyperbolic (covered by the disk). However, the precise topological classification of generic leaves on $\mathbb{P}^2$ remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Topology of generic foliations on Stein manifolds (Firsova)
status_evidence.snippet: For a generic foliation on Stein manifolds, all leaves except for at most countably many are contractible, with the rest being topological cylinders.
status_evidence.claim: A related result is known for generic foliations on Stein manifolds, but not for $\mathbb{P}^2$ specifically.

status_evidence.claim: The topology of generic leaves on $\mathbb{P}^2$ is listed as an open basic question.
